newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Exxon, Azeris may sign new Caspian oil deal in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Exxon, Azeris may sign new Caspian oil deal in 1997.

text.p: Azerbaijan and oil major Exxon Corp could sign a deal this year on developing three deep-water Caspian Sea offshore oilfields, an official at Azerbaijan's state oil company SOCAR said on Friday.

SOCAR official Daud Babayev told Reuters that a deal to develop the D-3, D-9 and D-38 fields "could not be excluded" in 1997. Exxon and SOCAR signed a memorandum of understanding on the project last year.
"We have made a proposal to Exxon on the three fields and we are waiting for a counter proposal from them," he said.

The three fields, each with estimated reserves of at least 50 million tonnes, are located about 100 km (60 miles) offshore from the capital Baku in water over 500 meters deep. The oil deposits are at a level of over 4,500 meters below the surface.
Exxon Chairman of the Board Lee Raymond visited Baku on Thursday and met with Azeri President Haydar Aliyev.
He later told reporters that Exxon had "unique experience and technology" in deep-water oil exploration and drilling which it would apply to Azerbaijan.
Aliyev said the former Soviet republic looked favourably upon further cooperation with Exxon.

The oil giant already has a share in the so-called "contract of the century" signed in 1994 with a Western consortium to develop three other Caspian fields. Consortium investment in that project is expected to eventually total $8 billion.
Azerbaijan has signed a series of major contracts, worth around $15 billion, with foreign oil firms to develop its massive offshore reserves.
